Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation expectations (post-call recap)

Tom / Megan — great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call around deployment mode and data isolation.

Key points we heard:
- Primary requirement: data must never be accessible to other customers or leave your control plane; strong preference for customer-managed networking and key management.
- Options discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (isolated compute but Redwood-managed control plane), Private VPC / on-prem (customer-managed control plane, network isolation).
- Requirements you flagged: HSM/KMS integration, no cross-tenant compute, control over log retention location, strict egress rules, SOC2/ISO evidence for our controls, and optional on-prem deployment for certain workloads.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-private-vpc-comparison.pdf (high-level differences), finsecure-mp-reqs.xlsx (your rough mapping we took on the call).

Questions / next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether your priority is: a) strict cryptographic and network isolation (Private VPC/on-prem) or b) dedicated GPU pools with Redwood-managed control plane (Dedicated)?
2) We can schedule an architecture deep dive with Rishi (solutions architect) to cover network topology, keyflow, logging/backups — suggested slots below.
3) Please share any compliance docs (exact SOC2 scope) or an NDA if you prefer before we share detailed implementation diagrams.

- We are leaning toward Private VPC (or on-prem) for our initial phase because we cannot have any possibility of customer cross-tenant access to sensitive PII.

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — technical notes and immediate answers

Tom / Megan — thanks for the context. Quick technical notes to address the items you raised and to help scope the architecture deep-dive.

Short answers:
- Private VPC: provides a customer-managed control plane and compute that runs in your VPC (or on-prem). No shared compute with other Redwood customers, and all network interfaces are in your account. Backups and logs can be written directly to your S3 buckets / CloudWatch — Redwood does not retain copies by default unless configured.
- Dedicated capacity: isolated GPU pools but the control plane (management plane) remains Redwood-managed. Data at rest/encrypt-in-transit is protected and per-tenant, but some metadata and control flows remain in Redwood’s control plane. This may not satisfy a strict ‘no managed control plane’ requirement.
- Key management: we support KMS/HSM integrations. For Private VPC we can integrate your KMS via customer-managed keys; for strict requirements we support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) with HSM-backed keys where available.
- Audit/loging: for Private VPC we can push logs to your destinations over private peering; for Dedicated we can arrange a delivery pipeline but retention in Redwood buckets is typical unless you opt-out.
- Network/egress: Private VPC gives you full control over outbound rules. We can also configure NAT gateways and restrict egress to specific endpoints.

Next steps I propose for the architecture call:
- Walk through a sample network diagram for Private VPC (we’ll bring a reference diagram).
- Confirm required firewall rules, peering steps, and subnet allocation.
- Demonstrate key-flow for BYOK/HSM and how we rotate keys.

I’ve attached a one-pager (redwood-vpc-onepager.pdf) that outlines the high-level architecture. I can lead the deep-dive; Marissa will coordinate scheduling. My availability (PST): Mon 11/22 10:00–12:00, Tue 11/23 14:00–16:00.
